findings_qualitative.value: A tight correlation exists between nuclear 1 mm luminosity, intrinsic 2-10 keV X-ray luminosity, and SMBH mass (the mm fundamental plane of BH accretion), holding for both low-luminosity and high-luminosity AGN.

evidence.quote: We report the discovery of the “mm fundamental plane of black-hole accretion”, which is a tight correlation between the nuclear 1 mm luminosity ( 𝐿 𝜈, mm ), the intrinsic 2 – 10 keV X-ray luminosity ( 𝐿 X , 2−10 ) and the supermassive black hole (SMBH) mass ( 𝑀 BH ) with an intrinsic scatter ( 𝜎 int ) of 0 . 40 dex.
Combining these sources with a sample of high-luminosity (quasar-like) nearby AGN, we show that the plane still holds.

findings_qualitative.value: Classic geometrically-thin accretion disc plus dusty torus models (SKIRTOR) fail to reproduce the observed mm luminosities by 2 to 4 orders of magnitude.

evidence.quote: The luminosities extracted from the torus models reasonably reproduces the slope of the 𝐿 X , 2−10 – 𝐿 𝜈, mm relation of the BASS sources, but with an offset of about two orders of magnitude at a given L bol .

On the other hand, to explain 𝐿 𝜈, mm of the lower accretion rate galaxies, the mm luminosities in the SKIRTOR models would need to be at least four orders of magnitude larger at a given accretion rate (and thus X-ray luminosity).

findings_qualitative.value: ADAF models naturally reproduce the slope and nearly edge-on projection of the mmFP (with a 0.5 dex offset in M_BH using default parameters), while compact jet models encompass most LLAGN but exhibit 3D curvature and require extra X-ray components for high-luminosity AGN.

evidence.quote: In Fig. 3b, we show the projection of the ADAF model grid onto the best-fitting mmFP. This latter seems to arise naturally from these models, as an (almost) edge-on view
The model grids encompass the majority of the LLAGN and some BASS sources, but they have significant curvature in the 3D 𝑀 BH - 𝐿 X , 2−10 𝐿 𝜈, mm space

claims.hypothesis: Nuclear 1 mm luminosity correlates tightly with SMBH mass and intrinsic 2-10 keV X-ray luminosity in nearby AGN, forming a millimetre fundamental plane of black hole accretion.
claims.experiment: Measured core 1 mm continuum luminosities from high-angular-resolution ALMA Band 6 images for 48 primary sample galaxies, compiled intrinsic 2-10 keV X-ray luminosities and SMBH masses, and fitted 1D and 2D regressions using lts_linefit and lts_planefit.
claims.result: Found a significant M_BH-L_nu,mm relation (sigma_int = 0.51 +/- 0.08 dex, rho = 0.79) and a tighter 3D plane M_BH-L_X,2-10-L_nu,mm (sigma_int = 0.40 +/- 0.07 dex, rho = 0.88, Delta BIC >> 10), which lowers to sigma_int = 0.11 dex when restricted to redshift-independent distances.
claims.finding: A tight mm fundamental plane of BH accretion exists and provides a rapid indirect method to estimate SMBH masses.

This led us to obtain much tighter correlations, with an intrinsic scatter of 0 _._ 19 dex for the _𝑀_ BH − _𝐿_ _𝜈,_ mm relation and only 0 _._ 11 dex for the mmFP.

claims.hypothesis: The mm fundamental plane defined primarily by LLAGN also holds for higher-luminosity, higher-accretion-rate (quasar-like) AGN.
claims.experiment: Overlaid 88 luminous AGN from the Swift-BAT AGN Spectroscopic Survey (BASS) with archival high-resolution ALMA 1 mm and nuclear X-ray data onto the best-fitting mmFP and performed a Spearman rank test.
claims.result: BASS sources agree with the best-fitting mmFP and show a statistically significant correlation (p = 0.002, rho = 0.32), though with larger scatter driven partly by indirect M_BH estimation methods.
claims.finding: The mmFP holds across both low-luminosity and high-luminosity AGN.

evidence.quote: As illustrated in Fig. 3b, the BASS sources are in agreement with the best-fitting mmFP, albeit with a larger observed scatter.

claims.hypothesis: Standard geometrically-thin accretion disc and dusty torus models can explain the nuclear mm and X-ray luminosities of the sample.
claims.experiment: Extrapolated SKIRTOR torus SED models across L_bol = 10^7.5 to 10^12.5 L_sun to 237.5 GHz and 2-10 keV and compared predicted luminosities with observations.
claims.result: Torus models underpredict L_nu,mm by about two orders of magnitude for BASS sources and by at least four orders of magnitude for lower-accretion-rate galaxies.
claims.finding: Classic torus-thin accretion disc models are ruled out as the driver of the observed mmFP.

evidence.quote: The luminosities extracted from the torus models reasonably reproduces the slope of the _𝐿_ X _,_ 2−10 – _𝐿_ _𝜈,_ mm relation of the BASS sources, but with an offset of about two orders of magnitude at a given L bol .

On the other hand, to explain _𝐿_ _𝜈,_ mm of the lower accretion rate galaxies, the mm luminosities in the SKIRTOR models would need to be at least four orders of magnitude larger at a given accretion rate (and thus X-ray luminosity).

claims.hypothesis: Radiatively-inefficient accretion flows (ADAFs) or compact radio jets explain the physical origin of the mmFP.
claims.experiment: Generated grids of SEDs from the Pesce et al. (2021) LLAGN ADAF model and the Lucchini et al. (2022) Bhjet compact jet model and compared predicted 237.5 GHz and 2-10 keV luminosities against the observed data.
claims.result: ADAF models naturally reproduce the slope and edge-on projection of the mmFP across both LLAGN and BASS samples (with a 0.5 dex offset for default parameters), while compact jet models cover most LLAGN but show significant 3D curvature and require additional X-ray components at high luminosities.
claims.finding: Radiatively-inefficient processes (ADAF-like flows or compact jets) likely play a key role in both low- and high-luminosity AGN, with ADAF models reproducing the relation more naturally.

evidence.quote: The ADAF models reproduces the observed relations somewhat better than those for compact jets, although neither provides a perfect fit.
In short, we demonstrated that ADAF-like models convincingly predict the mmFP. Compact jets are also a plausible explanation (at least for LLAGN)

As all the data were obtained with long-baseline configurations, extended dust emission is resolved out. We indeed typically detect only a point-like source at each galaxy centre, arising from unresolved core emission.

why_this_method.value: lts_linefit and lts_planefit combine least-trimmed-squares robust regression with least-squares fitting to account for intrinsic scatter and uncertainties in all coordinates.

evidence.quote: This combines the least-trimmed-squares (LTS) robust regression technique (Rousseeuw 1984) with a least-squares fitting algorithm, and allows for intrinsic scatter and uncertainties in all coordinates.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Classic dusty torus and thin accretion disc model (SKIRTOR) considered and rejected as the physical driver of the mmFP

evidence.quote: We thus conclude that, while “classic” torus models seem to be ruled out, either ADAF-like or compact jet emission have the potential to explain the observed trend.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Spurious correlation induced by galaxy distance uncertainties considered and rejected via Monte Carlo simulation and redshift-independent distance subsample test

evidence.quote: To test that this is not affecting our results, we performed a simple Monte Carlo simulation, drawing 𝑀 BH and the luminosities from independent Gaussian distributions that are truly uncorrelated, forcing a correlation to arise due to distance errors alone.
We thus conclude that our results are not biased due to distance uncertainties.

limitations_admitted.value: Primary sample is constructed based on data availability only and is not statistically complete.

evidence.quote: Crucially, although constructed based on data availability only (and thus not meant to be complete in any statistical sense), our primary sample spans four orders of magnitude in SMBH mass.

limitations_admitted.value: In 3 out of 48 galaxies, the central mm emission is slightly resolved, making their flux measurements more uncertain.

evidence.quote: In 3 (out of 48) galaxies, the emission is slightly resolved, making our measurements more uncertain.

limitations_admitted.value: Non-simultaneous nuclear mm and X-ray observations are subject to AGN time variability (factor of 2-3 over year timescales), which likely dominates the observed scatter.

evidence.quote: Since the nuclear mm and X-ray emission from AGN is known to be time variable (typically by a factor of 2 – 3 over year timescales; Prieto et al. 2016; Fernández-Ontiveros et al. 2019; Behar et al. 2020), variability likely dominates the observed scatters (and thus the underlying correlations may be tighter).

limitations_admitted.value: Five X-ray observed sources lack Chandra data and could have L_X,2-10 slightly overestimated due to diffuse hot gas or X-ray binaries.

evidence.quote: We also note that the 𝐿 X , 2−10 of the five X-ray observed sources without available Chandra data could be slightly overestimated, due to contamination from diffuse hot gas in the galactic and circum-galactic medium (CGM; although this mainly emits in the 0 . 3 – 2 keV range) and/or X-ray binaries.

limitations_admitted.value: Default ADAF model parameters overpredict L_nu,mm at a given SMBH mass by ~0.5 dex, and plasma physics parameters in both ADAF and compact jet models are poorly constrained.

evidence.quote: We note, however, that keeping the default model parameters from Pesce et al. (2021), the model well predicts the gradient of the mmFP, but is offset by a small amount (i.e. the model overpredicts 𝐿 𝜈, mm at a given SMBH mass by ≈ 0 . 5 dex).

We caution, however, that the plasma physics underlying both the ADAF and compact jet models is not well constrained, and significant uncertainties are present in all the model parameters and how they interact.

referee_caveats_inferred: Spatial resolution varies by nearly two orders of magnitude across the primary sample (6 to 330 pc), which could introduce aperture/resolution bias if sub-kpc dust or star formation contributes in the more distant or lower-resolution targets.

5 non-detections (upper limits) in L_nu,mm are listed in Table A1 (FRL1146, NGC3351, NGC3368, NGC5806, NGC6753), and the paper does not explicitly state how upper limits were treated in lts_linefit and lts_planefit (which standardly do not model censored data).

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA data available in the ALMA archive; X-ray data in Bi et al. (2020) or NED; calibrated data and final products shared upon reasonable request to the first author

evidence.quote: The ALMA data used in this article are all available to download at the ALMA archive ( https://almascience.nrao.edu/asax/ ).
The calibrated data, final products and original plots generated for this research study will be shared upon reasonable request to the first author.
The X-ray data have been retrieved from the catalogue of Bi et al. (2020) or from the NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED; https://ned.ipac.caltech.edu/ ).
